definition.simple: Tiny chemical helpers in your body that speed up the breaking down of food.
definition.academic: Biological catalysts, usually proteins, that significantly speed up the rate of virtually all of the chemical reactions that take place within cells, including digestion.

examples: Amylase in saliva breaking down starch
Pepsin in the stomach breaking down proteins

common_misconceptions: Enzymes are consumed during the reaction.
ai_context.tutor_hint: Compare enzymes to a pair of scissors cutting a long string of paper (complex food) into smaller pieces. The scissors don't get used up, they just do the cutting!
